resolutions.red_first: With the reviewer's mutation still in place, the FIXED walk exits 1 with 6 failures: `1024: #source is not visible (exclusion off) — box 349x636 at top 582, offsetParent=True …` and the same at 1024-on, 900-off/on, 768-off/on.
resolutions.fix: `Element.checkVisibility({visibilityProperty, opacityProperty, contentVisibilityAuto})`, not `offsetParent`. This is a deliberate departure from the finding's own suggested acceptance: `offsetParent !== null` and non-zero width/height BOTH stay true under `visibility:hidden`, so neither would have caught the reviewer's own mutation — the failure lines above record `offsetParent=True` on every one of the six. `offsetParent` is still recorded beside `visible` so a later reader can see where the two disagree. Both mutations were then checked: `visibility:hidden` -> 6 failures; `display:none!important` -> 7 (the extra one is the row-geometry check, since a display:none pane has no rect). Note for the record: a plain `display:none` without `!important` is INERT against this stylesheet — the later `#source{…display:flex…}` rule has equal specificity and wins — so the walk correctly reported no defect for it, and the mutation needed `!important` to be a real mutation.
resolutions.verified_after: Mutation removed, walk re-run: 0 failures, `panes_visible: true` at all four widths. The c13aa5c baseline was re-generated with the strengthened instrument and now reports 10 failures (was 9; the extra one is R1's new control).
